questions.question_text: Find the sum of the roots of the quadratic equation $x^{2}+9x-20=0$.

options.why: Used $+b/a$ instead of the correct $-b/a$ formula.
Confused the sum of roots with the constant term.
Confused the sum of roots with the negative of the constant term.

questions.question_text: What is the product of the roots of $5x^{2}-13x-7=0$?

options.why: Omitted the negative sign on the constant term $-7$.
Calculated the sum of roots $-b/a$ instead of the product.
Calculated the sum of roots with an incorrect sign.

questions.question_text: Find the product of the roots of $3x^{2}-8x=0$.

options.why: Calculated the linear term ratio instead of the constant term ratio.
Calculated the sum of the roots instead of the product.
Inverted the coefficient ratio and ignored the zero constant term.

questions.question_text: Which monic quadratic equation has roots $-3$ and $7$?

options.why: Used $+(\alpha+\beta)x$ instead of $-(\alpha+\beta)x$ in standard form.
Used the wrong sign for the product of roots $(-3)(7)=-21$.
Inverted the signs of both the sum and the product of roots.

questions.question_text: The equation $3x^{2}+kx-12=0$ has roots that sum to $-4$. What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Forgot the negative sign in the sum formula $\alpha+\beta=-b/a$.
Did not multiply by the leading coefficient $a=3$ when solving.
Assumed $k$ equals the sum of roots without dividing by $a$ or changing sign.

questions.question_text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $4x^{2}-7x+2=0$, find the value of $(\alpha+1)(\beta+1)$.

options.why: Calculated $(\alpha+\beta)+\alpha\beta$ without adding the constant $1$.
Used $+b/a=-7/4$ instead of $-b/a=7/4$ in the expanded expression.
Subtracted the product of roots instead of adding it.

questions.question_text: Find a monic quadratic equation with integer coefficients whose roots are $1+\sqrt{2}$ and $1-\sqrt{2}$.

options.why: Evaluated $(1+\sqrt{2})(1-\sqrt{2})$ as $1+2=3$ or mistaken square.
Used the wrong sign for the linear term $-(\alpha+\beta)x$.
Incorrectly computed the product of roots as $1-4=-3$.

questions.question_text: The quadratic equation $2x^{2}-10x+c=0$ has one root that is $4$ times the other. What is the value of $c$?

options.why: Forgot to multiply by the leading coefficient $a=2$ when solving for $c$.
Applied an incorrect negative sign to the product of roots.
Squared the sum of roots instead of using the ratio relationship.
